subject: PrivCP access orchestration: assertion handshake + role mapping kickoff

Subject: PrivCP access orchestration: assertion handshake + role mapping kickoff

Hi Priya / Ben —

Thanks for agreeing to kick off the Private Control Plane (PrivCP) identity integration. High-level goals for this thread:
- Confirm SAML assertion attributes Acme's IdP will send (group claims / role claims)
- Agree on SCIM provisioning attributes and whether we'll do full-provision or just delta sync
- Define operator vs delegated-admin role mappings and session durations for audit/compliance
- Nail down test plan and cutover windows (staging -> canary -> prod)

Attachments: acme_saml_metadata.xml (IdP metadata), scim_attribute_matrix.csv (draft)

Initial questions from our side:
1) Will you be able to include a groups claim with full AD path (e.g., "CN=RedwoodAdmins,OU=Apps,DC=acme,DC=com") or just group names?
2) For SCIM, do you plan to push users and groups from your IdP, or prefer us to pull with a read-only SCIM service account?
3) Any requirement for session lifetime > 1 hour for operator workflows? Our default SAML assertion TTL is 60 minutes.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Acme shares final IdP metadata (we got the draft attached) and confirms groups claim.
- We (Redwood) produce a role-mapping proposal and SCIM attribute mapping by EOD tomorrow.
- Schedule a 45m technical call (Marcus + Naomi + Acme SSO engineer) to test SAML handshake in staging next week.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from Acme's side:
- We can include both group names and the full AD distinguishedName in the groups claim, but that requires a small change to our outbound claim transform. We can enable it for the Redwood integration by next Tuesday.
- For SCIM we prefer push (IdP -> SCIM) for group membership changes. Our IdP can POST to a Redwood SCIM endpoint using a service account; please confirm the expected auth header format and whether you support x509 client cert auth for SCIM.
- Session lifetime: our security team prefers 2 hour assertions for operator workflows (they want longer session buffers for on-call tasks). They also require that we can revoke sessions via a SCIM delta of "disabled" flag for users.

Ben from Thirdwave (cc) will coordinate the IdP claim transform and attach a clean metadata file later today.

Folks —

Quick notes from product/security POV before Marcus & Naomi dive into the SAML/SCIM details:
- We should treat Acme's preferred 2hr operator session as an exception. That requires us to:
  * record explicit session TTLs in audit logs,
  * allow revocation via SCIM (user.disabled -> immediate session revocation), and
  * create a canary policy that prevents long sessions for newly onboarded accounts for first 7 days.
- Mapping model: propose three canonical PrivCP roles: "privcp_operator", "privcp_delegated_admin", "privcp_readonly". If Acme sends group names, we'll map groups -> these roles. If they send full DN, we'll support pattern-based mapping.
- SCIM model: prefer read-pull from Redwood for initial sync (to avoid accidental mass writes), then allow push-enabled deltas once we verify idempotency in staging.

I've attached a draft matrix (scim_attribute_matrix.csv) and a one-page role mapping PDF (privcp_role_mapping_proposal.pdf). Marcus: please confirm whether the control plane accepts role bindings scoped to org-level vs account-level. Naomi: can you validate logging fields we need for SOC2 evidence?

Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: PrivCP access orchestration: assertion handshake + role mapping kickoff

+1 on Laura's approach. A few implementation details and constraints:
- Role binding scope: PrivCP supports both org-level and account-level bindings. For Acme we recommend org-level bindings for "delegated_admin" and account-level for "operator" tasks (fine-grained).
- Assertion structure: prefer a dedicated attribute urn:redwood:roles containing comma-separated canonical role ids (e.g., privcp_delegated_admin,privcp_readonly). We can fall back to groups claim mapping, but code path is simpler with a roles claim.
- Session TTLs: 2 hours is okay if we add a session-revocation webhook that listens to SCIM user.disabled events. We'll accept a short-poll revocation window (<= 60s) for canary, and 5s webhook for prod if Acme can push webhooks.
- SCIM: we'll accept Bearer token auth for the initial push. We also support mutual TLS (mTLS) for SCIM endpoints — that's preferable for on-prem customers.

I'll schedule a 45m SAML handshake + SCIM test next Tuesday 8/26 at 10:00 PT. Marcus

Marcus Lin
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — plan and next steps captured below for clarity:

1) Acme to finalize IdP claim transforms and send the cleaned acme_saml_metadata-v2.xml (Priya/Ben) — target: Mon 8/25 EOD.
2) Redwood to lock role->binding table and test-mode mapping (Jasmine + Marcus) — deliverable: role mapping JSON + test harness by Mon 8/25 EOD. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PrivCP-Designs-Acme
3) SCIM approach: start with Redwood read-pull in staging (to validate shape) then enable push with Bearer token (Acme) in canary. If Acme prefers mTLS we can flip to mTLS for prod.
4) Session TTL: accept 2 hour operator session as exception, but require SCIM-based revocation to invalidate active sessions. Rishi, please own the revocation webhook SLA and monitoring (SOC2 evidence).
5) Test window: SAML handshake + SCIM pull test on Tue 8/26 10:00 PT (45m). Marcus/Naomi/Acme IdP engineer to attend.

Action owners: Jasmine (test harness + docs), Marcus (SAML/SCIM endpoint config), Rishi (revocation webhook + monitoring), Priya/Ben (IdP metadata + claim transform).

If there are no objections I'll create the follow-up calendar invite and open JIRA SECOPS-4421 to track the cutover checklist.

Cheers,
Jasmine
